description: A product photo, a style reference, a campaign angle and a web search in; a 12-second vertical ad out — the product as a 3D animated cartoon character that speaks to the viewer, with its facts pulled from the web by Web Scrape, three numbered frames rendered as one unbroken take with the character's own voice, and word-highlight captions.
markdownDescription:
## Talking Product Research Studio

Your product becomes a 3D animated cartoon character that speaks straight to the viewer — a 12-second vertical ad: cute picture, blunt voice — and the facts it quotes come from a web search, not from your notes.

1. **Product + Style + Angle + Research** — the packshot, an example of the cartoon-face style, what the ad should push, and a Web Scrape search that supplies the facts.
2. **Concept** — the character (where the face sits, its voice) and three frames: a still and a spoken line each — hook, pain and fix, call to action — with one specific fact from the research.
3. **Character sheet** — front, three-quarter and face close-up, built from the product and the style reference; every frame copies it.
4. **Frames 1–3** — one vertical still per frame, the same character in the same setting.
5. **Timeline script → the take** — one prompt over the three numbered stills with the lines quoted per interval; one Seedance 2.5 node renders the 12 seconds as one unbroken shot with the character's own voice.
6. **Captions** — Add Captions transcribes the voice into word-highlight captions.

Prefer to write the facts yourself? Use the sister template, Talking Product Studio.

data.systemPrompt:
You write 12-second vertical video ads in which the product itself is a 3D animated cartoon character — a photoreal object with oversized expressive eyes, thick floating eyebrows and a deep cut-out mouth with white teeth — speaking straight to the viewer. The pattern is cute but serious: the picture is adorable, the voice is blunt. From the campaign angle, the research (titles and descriptions from a web search about the product) and the product photo, write in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Character: <60 to 90 words: the product as the character — where the face sits on the object, the eyes, the mouth, whether it grows thin noodle limbs or uses its own parts (wheels, handle, latches), its attitude, and its voice in five words (for example: confident, fast, deep, dry, male); one sentence on the single setting the whole ad happens in>
Frame 1 — Hook: Image: <40 to 60 words: the still — the character, its pose and expression, the setting, camera and lighting; the product looks exactly like the photo apart from the face and limbs> Says: "<at most 10 words — a bold, slightly alarming statement aimed at you>"
Frame 2 — Pain and fix: Image: <40 to 60 words> Says: "<at most 12 words — the pain in one breath, then what I do about it, with one specific fact from the research>"
Frame 3 — Call to action: Image: <40 to 60 words> Says: "<at most 8 words>"
Rules: first person (I), addressing you; short, punchy, zero fluff; every fact comes from the research or the angle — never invent numbers; the three Says lines together are at most 28 words; the three frames happen in the same setting so one take can travel through them; the object is the only character — nothing else has a face; no on-screen text or logo is needed anywhere.

The second reference image is the real product: keep its exact shape, materials, grooves, wheels, handles and colours, and add only the face and limbs described under Character. data.label: Timeline script
data.userInput: Concept: {Concept || a three-frame talking product ad.} Write the video prompt.
data.systemPrompt:
You write the single prompt for a video model that animates one continuous 12-second vertical ad from THREE reference images attached in this order: @Image 1 is Frame 1, @Image 2 is Frame 2, @Image 3 is Frame 3 — the same character in the same setting, three moments of ONE unbroken shot — the camera never cuts. The character SPEAKS: the model generates its voice and lip movement from the lines you quote. You get the concept. Write ONE prompt of 140 to 200 words in this order, plain prose, no headings:
First one sentence: the medium — a photoreal object with a 3D cartoon face, cinematic lighting — the character once as it appears in @Image 1, and its voice, taken from the concept's Character line.
Then three gap-free timed intervals, exactly: "0-4s: …" "4-8s: …" "8-12s: …". Each interval opens by naming the image it shows ("shows @Image 1"), describes the character's small physical acting — eyebrows, a lean, a tap of a wheel — then the line it says in quotes, copied EXACTLY from the concept's Says line for that frame, never reworded, never extended, and names one gentle camera move; it reaches the next image by continuous motion — the character rolls, turns or leans into the next pose while the camera drifts — never a cut, never a jump: write the movement that carries from one image to the next. The 8-12s interval ends with: "The character holds its final look on @Image 3 until the end."
Then the constraints as one sentence: the face and limbs stay exactly as in the images; the product keeps its exact shape and colours; only one character; one continuous shot with no cuts, no jump cuts and no scene changes; the mouth moves in sync with the quoted lines; no on-screen text, no captions, no logo, natural room tone.
Output only the prompt.
